addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

input.prompt:
I need to trace how a browser request for another user's profile image (avatar) is served in this repository — from the HTTP route handler all the way down to stored data. Search very thoroughly for:

1. Routes/handlers related to user profile images, avatars, or profile pictures (look for URL patterns like /avatar, /photo, /picture, /image in route definitions)
2. The handler function that serves these images
3. Each function call or hop from that handler down to the data/storage layer

Look in files related to routing, user profiles, avatars, image serving. Check for patterns like "avatar", "profile_image", "profile_picture", "user_image", "photo", "picture" in route definitions, handler files, service files, and storage/data access files.

Report every file path, function/method name, and how each layer calls the next. Be very thorough — search across the entire codebase.

content.text: I now have all the information needed to provide a comprehensive trace. Here is the complete report. --- ## Complete Request Trace: Browser Request for Another User's Avatar ### Overview This is the **Memos** application (Go, using the Echo web framework). The avatar serving flow goes through an HTTP file server, not the gRPC/Connect API stack. Avatars are stored inline in the database as base64-encoded data URIs in the `avatar_url` column of the `user` table. --- ### Layer 1: Server Bootstrap and Route Registration **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/server.go` (lines 79-82) The main server creates a `FileServerService` and registers its routes on the Echo instance: ```go fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret) fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer) ``` **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 111-125) `NewFileServerService` builds the service struct, wiring in an `Authenticator` and the store. `RegisterRoutes` registers the HTTP route: ```go func (s *FileServerService) RegisterRoutes(echoServer *echo.Echo) { fileGroup := echoServer.Group("/file") fileGroup.GET("/users/:identifier/avatar", s.serveUserAvatar) } ``` The URL pattern is: **`GET /file/users/{username}/avatar`** --- ### Layer 2: HTTP Handler -- `serveUserAvatar` **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 167-210) Method: `func (s *FileServerService) serveUserAvatar(c *echo.Context) error` This handler performs the following steps: 1. **Authentication check (private instances)** -- calls `s.Profile.AllowAnonymous()`. If the instance is private (no `InstanceURL` configured), it calls `s.getCurrentUser(ctx, c)` to verify the requesting user is authenticated. Anonymous requests get HTTP 401. 2. **Extract the `:identifier` path parameter** -- this is the target user's username. 3. **Look up the target user** -- calls `s.getUserByUsername(ctx, identifier)`. 4. **Check avatar existence** -- if `user.AvatarURL` is empty, returns HTTP 404. 5. **Parse the data URI** -- calls `s.parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL)` to extract MIME type and raw image bytes from the `data:image/png;base64,...` string. 6. **Validate MIME type** -- checks against `avatarAllowedTypes` (png, jpeg, jpg, gif, webp, heic, heif). 7. **Serve the image** -- sets security headers (`X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, CSP), `Content-Type`, and `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600`, then returns the binary blob via `c.Blob()`. --- ### Layer 3: Authentication -- `getCurrentUser` **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 708-712) ```go func (s *FileServerService) getCurrentUser(ctx context.Context, c *echo.Context) (*store.User, error) { authHeader := c.Request().Header.Get(echo.HeaderAuthorization) cookieHeader := c.Request().Header.Get("Cookie") return s.authenticator.AuthenticateToUser(ctx, authHeader, cookieHeader) } ``` This delegates to the shared `Authenticator`. **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/auth/authenticator.go` (lines 190-208) Method: `func (a *Authenticator) AuthenticateToUser(ctx context.Context, authHeader, cookieHeader string) (*store.User, error)` Authentication priority: 1. Bearer token from `Authorization` header (Access Token V2 or PAT) -- resolved via `a.resolveBearer()` (line 191). 2. Refresh token from `Cookie` header -- resolved via `a.AuthenticateByRefreshToken()` (line 202). Both paths ultimately call `a.store.GetUser()` to load the authenticated user from the database. --- ### Layer 4: Privacy Check -- `AllowAnonymous` **File:** `/bench/home/work/internal/profile/profile.go` (lines 39-48) ```go func (p *Profile) AllowAnonymous() bool { return strings.TrimSpace(p.InstanceURL) != "" } ``` If `InstanceURL` is set, the instance is "open" and anonymous avatar access is allowed. If blank, the instance is "private" and authentication is required. --- ### Layer 5: User Lookup -- `getUserByUsername` **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 715-717) ```go func (s *FileServerService) getUserByUsername(ctx context.Context, identifier string) (*store.User, error) { return s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier}) } ``` This calls `Store.GetUser` with a `FindUser` filter that sets only the `Username` field. --- ### Layer 6: Store Layer -- `Store.GetUser` **File:** `/bench/home/work/store/user.go` (lines 148-169) ```go func (s *Store) GetUser(ctx context.Context, find *FindUser) (*User, error) { if find.ID != nil { if cache, ok := s.userCache.Get(ctx, userCacheKey(*find.ID)); ok { user, ok := cache.(*User) if ok { return user, nil } } } list, err := s.ListUsers(ctx, find) if err != nil { return nil, err } if len(list) == 0 { return nil, nil } user := list[0] s.userCache.Set(ctx, userCacheKey(user.ID), user) return user, nil } ``` In the avatar flow, the lookup is by username (not ID), so the cache check on line 149 is skipped. It falls through to `s.ListUsers()`. --- ### Layer 7: Store Layer -- `Store.ListUsers` **File:** `/bench/home/work/store/user.go` (lines 136-146) ```go func (s *Store) ListUsers(ctx context.Context, find *FindUser) ([]*User, error) { list, err := s.driver.ListUsers(ctx, find) // ... for _, user := range list { s.userCache.Set(ctx, userCacheKey(user.ID), user) } return list, nil } ``` This delegates to the database driver interface and populates the user cache on the way back. --- ### Layer 8: Database Driver Interface **File:** `/bench/home/work/store/driver.go` (lines 47-48) The `Driver` interface requires: ```go ListUsers(ctx context.Context, find *FindUser) ([]*User, error) ``` Three implementations exist: #### SQLite Driver **File:** `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/user.go` (lines 88-205) The `ListUsers` method builds a `SELECT` query against the `user` table. When `find.Username` is set, it adds `WHERE username = ?`. The query selects the `avatar_url` column (line 159) and scans it into `user.AvatarURL` (line 189). #### PostgreSQL Driver **File:** `/bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/user.go` Same pattern -- selects `avatar_url` from the `user` table, scans into `user.AvatarURL`. #### MySQL Driver **File:** `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/user.go` Same pattern -- selects `avatar_url` from the `user` table, scans into `user.AvatarURL`. --- ### Layer 9: Data URI Parsing **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` (lines 737-750) ```go var dataURIRegex = regexp.MustCompile(`^data:(?P[^;]+);base64,(?P.+)`) func (*FileServerService) parseDataURI(dataURI string) (string, []byte, error) { matches := dataURIRegex.FindStringSubmatch(dataURI) if len(matches) != 3 { return "", nil, errors.New("invalid data URI format") } imageType := matches[1] imageData, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(matches[2]) // ... return imageType, imageData, nil } ``` The `avatar_url` column stores a complete data URI (e.g., `data:image/png;base64,iVBOR...`). This method extracts the MIME type and decodes the base64 payload into raw bytes. --- ### Layer 10: Cache Layer **File:** `/bench/home/work/store/cache/cache.go` The `Store` has a `userCache` field of type `*cache.Cache` (configured with 10-minute TTL, 1000 max items). After the first DB lookup, subsequent calls to `GetUser` with the same user ID will hit the cache. However, the avatar flow looks up by username, so only after the result is fetched and cached by ID would a subsequent ID-based lookup benefit. --- ### How the Avatar URL Reaches the Browser There is a second, complementary path: when the frontend fetches user profile data via the gRPC/Connect API. **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go` (lines 16-42) The `convertUserFromStore` function converts a `store.User` into a protobuf `User` message. For the `AvatarUrl` field: ```go if user.AvatarURL != "" { _, _, err := extractImageInfo(user.AvatarURL) if err == nil { userpb.AvatarUrl = fmt.Sprintf("/file/%s/avatar", userpb.Name) } else { userpb.AvatarUrl = user.AvatarURL } } ``` If the avatar is a data URI (base64), the API response replaces it with the file-server URL `/file/users/{username}/avatar` to avoid sending large base64 blobs in every API response. If the avatar is an external URL (e.g., from SSO), it is passed through as-is. `userpb.Name` is built by `BuildUserName(user.Username)` which produces `users/{username}`. So the browser receives `avatarUrl: "/file/users/johndoe/avatar"` in the user protobuf response, and the frontend `` tag fetches that URL, triggering the file server flow described above. **File:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx` (line 14) ```tsx src={avatarUrl || "/full-logo.webp"} ``` --- ### ACL / Public Access **File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go` (line 25) The gRPC procedure `/memos.api.v1.UserService/GetUserAvatar` is listed in `PublicMethods`, meaning the API endpoint that returns user data (including the avatar URL) does not require authentication. However, it is NOT in `AuthBootstrapMethods`, so on a private instance anonymous callers cannot reach it. The file-server handler independently enforces the same policy: on a private instance, `serveUserAvatar` requires authentication (lines 173-181). --- ### Summary Call Chain ``` Browser GET /file/users/{username}/avatar | v Echo router --> fileserver.FileServerService.serveUserAvatar() | |--> [if private instance] FileServerService.getCurrentUser() | --> auth.Authenticator.AuthenticateToUser() | --> resolveBearer() or AuthenticateByRefreshToken() | --> store.Store.GetUser() [for the viewer] | |--> FileServerService.getUserByUsername(ctx, identifier) | --> store.Store.GetUser(ctx, &FindUser{Username: &identifier}) | --> store.Store.ListUsers() | --> driver.ListUsers() [sqlite/postgres/mysql] | --> SQL: SELECT ... avatar_url ... FROM user WHERE username = ? | --> userCache.Set() [cache the result] | --> return user (with user.AvatarURL = "data:image/png;base64,...") | |--> FileServerService.parseDataURI(user.AvatarURL) | --> regex extract MIME type + base64 decode to []byte | |--> avatarAllowedTypes check | |--> setSecurityHeaders() |--> c.Blob(200, imageType, imageData) | v Browser receives raw image bytes with correct Content-Type ``` ### Key Files (absolute paths) | Layer | File | |-------|------| | Server bootstrap | `/bench/home/work/server/server.go` | | Route registration + HTTP handler | `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go` | | Authentication | `/bench/home/work/server/auth/authenticator.go` | | Token extraction | `/bench/home/work/server/auth/extract.go` | | Privacy check | `/bench/home/work/internal/profile/profile.go` | | ACL config (public methods) | `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/acl_config.go` | | Avatar URL rewriting (API response) | `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go` | | Store: User model + GetUser/ListUsers | `/bench/home/work/store/user.go` | | Store: Driver interface | `/bench/home/work/store/driver.go` | | Store: Cache | `/bench/home/work/store/cache/cache.go` | | DB driver (SQLite) | `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/user.go` | | DB driver (PostgreSQL) | `/bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/user.go` | | DB driver (MySQL) | `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/user.go` | | Frontend component | `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/UserAvatar.tsx` | | Tests | `/bench/home/work/server/router/fileserver/fileserver_test.go` |
